source: Summarised from the Wilderness Medical Society altitude illness guidelines (2019 update) and Himachal Pradesh tourism safety advisories. This is not a substitute for medical advice.

altitude.intro: Altitude illness can affect anyone above about 2,500 m, however fit they are. It's preventable: go up slowly.
prevent: Above 3,000 m, raise your sleeping altitude by no more than 500 m a night.
Take a rest day for every 1,000 m you gain, or every 3–4 days.
Climb high, sleep low: day hikes higher than camp help you adjust.
Drink 3–4 litres of water a day. Skip alcohol and sleeping pills for the first nights up high.
Acetazolamide (Diamox) can help prevent it, but only take it on a doctor's advice.

levels.name: Mild altitude sickness (AMS)
levels.signs: Headache plus at least one of: nausea, tiredness, dizziness, poor sleep.
levels.action: Don't go higher. Rest, drink water, take paracetamol. Descend if it isn't better in 24 hours.

levels.name: Fluid on the lungs (HAPE)
levels.signs: Breathless even at rest, a cough (sometimes frothy or pink), blue lips, unusual tiredness.
levels.action: Emergency: descend at least 300–1,000 m now, with someone. Call 112. Give oxygen if you have it.

levels.name: Fluid on the brain (HACE)
levels.signs: Confusion, unusual behaviour, can't walk in a straight line, extreme drowsiness.
levels.action: Emergency: descend immediately with help. Call 112. Never leave the person alone.

altitude.rule: Never go higher with symptoms. Descend if they get worse. Most people recover quickly once they go down.

tell_someone: Share your itinerary: route, campsites and the date and time you expect to be back.
Agree a check-in time. If they don't hear from you by then, they call 112 and the local police.
Leave the names and phone numbers of your guide, operator or homestay.
Note where mobile signal ends (and which network works) on your route.
Carry a charged power bank, a whistle and a headlamp. Pair your OFFGRID beacon if you have one.
Register at the police post or forest check-post if there is one at the trailhead.
weather_rules: In the hills, afternoon storms build fast. Start early and be off exposed ridges by early afternoon.
After heavy rain, give roads and river crossings a day to settle. Landslides often come after the rain stops.
In thunder, get off ridges and summits. Avoid lone trees and metal poles; crouch on your pack if caught in the open.
